landing.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
landing.faq.description: Everything you need to know before getting started.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.
landing.cta.headline: Ready to ship your SaaS?
landing.cta.subheadline: Stop wiring auth, payments, and RBAC from scratch. Start with ShipAny Next and build what actually makes your product unique.

opus.story.title: Meet opus55video.
opus.story.intro.one: opus55video is an online workspace for creating videos from text. Start with a simple scene description, then add the people, setting, action, lighting, and camera movement that matter to your idea. Choose a frame format and duration that suit where the video will be seen. A fleeting cinematic image or a visual concept for your team can begin as a few lines of writing and become a moving shot you can watch.
opus.story.intro.two: You can begin without setting up a camera or editing project. Open the video studio, enter a prompt, choose landscape, portrait, or square framing, and set the shot to five or ten seconds. Once you submit the request, follow its progress in your creation history. When it is ready, review the result and return to your prompt to explore another pace, composition, or mood. Nothing is installed and nothing is prepared in advance; the opus55video studio is ready when the idea arrives.
opus.story.intro.three: The creative direction stays with you. Decide what appears in the frame, how the subject moves, and what the moment should feel like. AI translates those written cues into motion. Results vary with the prompt and generation process, so each attempt is also an opportunity to discover a new visual direction. That loop of writing and watching is the heart of the opus55video experience.
opus.story.intro.four: New models and styling options reach the opus55video studio as they become available, so the way your ideas look keeps evolving with the platform. What stays constant is the workflow: write, direct, generate, and refine in one place.
opus.story.use.title: Tell different stories with AI video
opus.story.use.one.title: Social video and short film ideas
opus.story.use.one.description: Looking for an opening shot for vertical content? Use opus55video to try a character, setting, and pace before choosing the direction for your story. Even a few seconds can establish a place or emotion, giving you a visual reference for a script, storyboard, or content pitch, and a fast way to test a look before you commit a shoot day.
opus.story.use.two.title: Brand and product concepts
opus.story.use.two.description: Turn an abstract proposal into a specific scene before full production. Where is the product? How does the camera approach it? Where does the light enter? An opus55video clip gives the team a shared image, so visual directions are easier to compare and a written idea is easier to discuss before any budget is spent.
opus.story.use.three.title: Personal visual experiments
opus.story.use.three.description: From science fiction landscapes to quiet portraits, rainy streets, and surreal spaces, a text prompt is a starting point for visual exploration. Change the time of day, weather, color, or camera move and see how one idea can produce different viewing experiences. Every opus55video result stays one click away, so you can compare directions side by side.
opus.story.guide.title: How do you write a clearer video prompt?
opus.story.guide.one: Begin with the subject and setting, then describe the action. Instead of only writing “a city at night,” try “a person in a dark coat crossing a neon-lit street after rain.” Specific details give the shot a clear moment to build around and make it easier to judge whether the result matches your intention.
opus.story.guide.two: Next, add camera direction and atmosphere. Does the camera push in slowly or follow the subject? Is the frame wide and still or close to a face? Is the light soft or high contrast? You do not need to include every detail at once. Define the elements that matter most, review the result, and adjust one or two things at a time.
opus.story.guide.three: Framing changes the way a shot feels. Landscape gives room to environments and spatial relationships. Portrait works well for a person or close view on a phone. Square framing can hold attention on a centered subject. Choose five seconds for a simple action, or ten seconds to allow more time for mood and camera movement. opus55video keeps these choices together in one workspace, so the format matches the platform where the shot will live.
opus.story.faq.title: Questions about opus55video
opus.story.faq.one.question: What can I use opus55video for?
opus.story.faq.one.answer: Use opus55video to turn written concepts into short video shots for creative exploration, storyboard references, social content ideas, and conversations about visual direction. Results depend on your prompt and the generation process, so trying a few variations on opus55video can help clarify the image you want. Keep the prompt close to what you would tell a cinematographer: who is in the frame, what happens, and how the camera behaves.
opus.story.faq.two.question: Do I need an image before generating a video?
opus.story.faq.two.answer: The current opus55video studio creates video from text. Enter a scene description of at least ten characters, choose a format and duration, and submit your request. A clear subject, action, and camera direction usually communicate more than style words alone.
opus.story.faq.three.question: Which formats and durations are available?
opus.story.faq.three.answer: opus55video offers landscape, portrait, and square framing with a five or ten second duration. Think about where the video will be viewed, such as a wide display, a phone, or a square content slot, before selecting the ratio. The opus55video studio shows every option before you submit.
opus.story.faq.four.question: Where do I find a video after submitting it?
opus.story.faq.four.answer: See recent requests and their status in the Your creations area of the opus55video studio. Generation can take several minutes. Once a request is complete, open the video and use what you learned to shape your next prompt.
opus.story.faq.five.question: Does opus55video cost anything to try?
opus.story.faq.five.answer: The public opus55video studio is free to try with a daily usage limit, and no account is needed. If paid plans arrive later, the price and billing terms will be shown before any purchase.
